leads.summary: Disabled dropdowns guard only their triggers, not already-open option actions
leads.consequence: If a popup was opened and the owning control is then disabled, directly invoking an existing option delegate's Accessible press/toggle action can still change the selected value or selection and emit changed. The new disabled-composite test only presses initially disabled, closed triggers, so it cannot catch this boundary. Whether a disabled popup remains exposed through a particular AT-SPI client requires a real desktop, but the direct QML action paths are unguarded.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus (opus/followup-1.md) confirmed by headless run plan-fu1; published as Optional N1, noting no shipped caller reaches it

leads.summary: Default Arch quickshell package is still 0.3.1, below the PR's required accessibility fix
leads.consequence: An uncustomized Omarchy installation following this package list receives the standard Arch quickshell package, whose current PKGBUILD is v0.3.1. The PR explicitly says v0.3.1 publishes no accessibility tree and requires commit 916a0dd, so merging the shell code alone does not make these controls available to the screen reader on the default installed version. Document an actual upgrade/install path, require a compatible build, or sequence this behind the package update. This is a dependency rollout gap, not evidence that the QML bindings are wrong.
leads.triage: factual and already stated in the PR body (inert on 0.3.1, needs 916a0dd); dropped as not new

leads.summary: The new checkable monitor-row fixture is a manually hardcoded stand-in, not MonitorRow
leads.consequence: Removing or breaking the actual Display panel MonitorRow checked binding would still pass this test: it constructs a generic CursorSurface with hardcoded checked:true/selected:false and asserts those same literals. The fixture does not check whether display.enabled controls the value or whether focus stays out of selected.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (mutation m-monitor passes); corroboration, published in Optional test improvement

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13212#issuecomment-5838150158), checked at `3ace0a2`.

**Verified:** all eight points from the earlier review are addressed. One detail of the earlier comment was wrong (see the correction below).

| Earlier point | Status on `3ace0a2` |
|---|---|
| Clock button named by its right-click hint | Resolved: named "Clock", hint exposed as description |
| Accessibility actions fire on disabled controls | Resolved: `Toggle`, `ToggleSwitch`, the dropdown triggers and `PanelSlider` ignore them while disabled |
| Display rows expose focus as "selected" | Resolved: rows expose on/off as checkable/checked, `selected` is false |
| AT-SPI value write skips `moved`/`released` | Resolved: the `accessibleItem` proxy commits writes through `moved`/`released` and keeps the caller's binding |
| Tailscale peer rows unnamed | Resolved: rows are named by the peer |
| Bar buttons expose no state | Resolved: a tooltip that differs from the name becomes the description (for example Network's "Limited internet access") |
| Docs: "no second code path" | Resolved: scoped to enabled controls, with the disabled and value-write cases described |
| Docs: "newer than 0.3.1" | Resolved: now names `916a0dd` |

The updated runtime fixture was run headlessly (compositor gate and `KeyboardPanel` check removed) on Quickshell 0.3.1 with Qt 6.11.2, alongside extra checks of the slider proxy. The fixture passes on this head and fails when any one of these is removed: the new disabled guards (except the `ToggleSwitch` press guard, see below), the proxy's commit, or its mirroring of the caller's value. The proxy starts at the caller's value (including one set after creation), snaps integer values, clamps out-of-range writes and reverts writes while disabled. No binding-loop warnings appeared. The `NetworkRow` change keeps the same behavior and makes `network-test.sh` pass again (it failed on the previous head). Across `test/shell.d`, every test file shared with the merge-base gives the same result on both.

**Correction to the earlier review:** it said the Weather bar button's "visible temperature" was not exposed. The Weather bar button shows a condition icon, not a temperature, and its tooltip is intentionally empty, so there was no temperature to lose. It still reads as "Weather", and the new description line does not change that.

**Optional test improvement:** three of the new behaviors can be removed without the fixture failing. It calls only the toggle action on the disabled `ToggleSwitch`, so removing its press guard still passes. Nothing checks the new `WidgetButton` description. The "DP-2" row is a stand-in `CursorSurface` with fixed `checked`/`selected` values, so removing the three lines from `monitor/Panel.qml` still passes. Pressing the disabled switch, asserting a `WidgetButton` description, and checking the `MonitorRow` bindings to `display.enabled` would cover them.

**Optional:** a `Dropdown`, `SearchableDropdown` or `MultiSelect` popup that is already open stays open when the control is disabled. A popup opened with `open()` also works on a disabled control. In both cases the option rows' accessibility actions still change the selection and emit `changed`. Their mouse areas stay enabled too, so the pointer should behave the same. A headless check showed the accessibility-action part for all three controls. No shipped caller disables these controls, so this only affects code outside the shipped shell, such as plugins. Closing the popup when `enabled` becomes false and guarding `open()`/`toggle()` would make "disabled controls ignore accessibility actions" hold for open popups too.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** pinned head `3ace0a2` against merge-base `7b336b1`, compared with the previously reviewed `19d5722`. The runtime fixture (modified as described), targeted mutation and diagnostic fixtures, and every `test/shell.d` file ran in an isolated headless runtime on Quickshell 0.3.1 with Qt 6.11.2. No screen reader, AT-SPI session or Quickshell build that includes `916a0dd` was run. AT-SPI behavior is inferred from Qt 6.11.2 source.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
